tx.t: Today I would like to outline what glaciers are, and why they matter for sea level. Glaciers cover about ten per cent of the world's land area.
Together, glaciers and ice sheets store about two thirds of the world's fresh water. A glacier forms when snow builds up for many years and is pressed into dense ice.
Since nineteen hundred, the global sea level has risen by about twenty centimetres. This rise is caused partly by melting ice and partly because warm water takes up more space.

tx.t: In this lecture I will describe how honeybees live and why they matter so much to farmers. A single summer hive can contain up to sixty thousand bees, but only one queen.

The queen can lay as many as two thousand eggs in one day. Worker bees live for only about six weeks in summer, and they spend their lives doing different jobs, from cleaning the hive to collecting nectar.
In its whole life, one worker produces only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey. Many crops, such as almonds and apples, depend on bees to carry pollen from flower to flower.

tx.t: In this talk I will explain what psychologists know about memory and how students can use it. In eighteen eighty-five, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the forgetting curve.

He found that people forget roughly half of new material within an hour if they do not review it. Reviewing material at increasing intervals, which is called spaced repetition, helps to move it into long-term memory.
Testing yourself is more effective than simply reading your notes again. A good night of sleep after studying helps to store what you have learned.

tx.t: Today I would like to describe a bike-sharing scheme in the town of Kingsley. It began in twenty fourteen with seven hundred and fifty-six bikes, placed at stations around the centre.
Use grew quickly. Within three years the number of journeys had risen by fifty per cent, and on a busy day there were more than twenty-one thousand trips.
The scheme soon met a serious problem: too few bikes in the hills. The council solved it with a van that moves bikes uphill every morning.
Today, a ride costs two pounds eighty for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.
